one_line: Rival kings at the turning point between the Rashtrakuta fall and the rise of the Western Chalukyas in the Deccan, c. 972–973 CE.

appearance.age_look: Tailapa appears in his late 30s, lean and battle-hardened; Karka appears in his early 30s, slightly broader in build but refined.
appearance.face: Both share medium-brown Deccan complexions and sharp jawlines; Tailapa has a narrow, angular face with a faint scar on his left cheek and intense, focused eyes, while Karka’s face is slightly rounder with calm, proud eyes; default expression for Tailapa is determined and alert, for Karka dignified and controlled, hinting at strain.
appearance.hair: Tailapa’s hair is long, black and tied into a high, tight warrior topknot (shikha-like knot) with a plain dark-red cloth band; a narrow gold forehead strip (simple mukuta band) sits low over the brow; Karka’s hair is also long, black and smoother, pulled back into a lower, thicker knot wrapped with a pale-gold band, topped with a modest, conical, cloth-covered crown cap with a small central red stone.
appearance.costume: Tailapa wears a practical Deccan warrior-king ensemble: a knee-length, deep-indigo cotton angarakha-style tunic crossing left over right with a subtle diagonal wrap and tied with internal ties, worn over a cream, close-fitting inner shirt with long sleeves; a wide, brick-red cotton sash (kati-bandha) wraps tightly around his waist, its end hanging to the left; below, he wears straight, ankle-length, dull-ochre cotton trousers with a slight taper; on top, over his torso, a sleeveless quilted cotton vamsha-padded vest in muted brown, stitched in vertical channels, adds subtle protection without fantasy plating; his feet have dark-brown leather sandals with toe loops and a mid-foot strap; jewellery is restrained—simple gold karnaphula earrings shaped like small discs, two slim gold bangles on each wrist, and a single rudraksha-style bead necklace; around his shoulders, a deep-maroon cotton uttariya (shawl) with a thin mustard border is draped from the left shoulder across the chest and thrown back behind the right arm, leaving his torso fully and modestly covered yet allowing arm movement. Karka wears a more courtly Rashtrakuta royal outfit: a finely woven off-white cotton dhoti wrapped in the Deccan style, pleated in front and reaching the ankles, with a wide dark-green border featuring a simple repeating geometric pattern; above, he wears a light-mustard, long-sleeved, waist-length cotton tunic (kurtaka) with a round neck and a short front slit tied with a small cord, the sleeves edged with a narrow maroon border; draped over both shoulders and across the chest is a rich, deep-green uttariya of soft cotton with a subtle gold-thread edge, creating a diagonal from right shoulder to left hip and covering his torso; his feet are in dark-tan leather sandals with slightly upturned toes; his jewellery is more ornate but still plausible: medium-sized gold disc earrings, a short gold necklace with three small pendants, a narrow gold armlet on each upper arm engraved with simple patterns, and two broader bangles per wrist.
appearance.signature: Tailapa’s signature weapon is a well-balanced, slightly curved, single-edged Deccan sword (similar to an early talwar) with a plain iron blade, a simple cross-guard, and a brown leather-wrapped grip, carried in a dark-brown leather scabbard hanging from his left side on a modest, functional belt; Karka’s signature prop is a long, polished palm-leaf charter roll bound with a red cord, symbolising royal grants and authority, which he holds or tucks under his right arm.

ref_desc: Tailapa II is a lean, scar-cheeked Deccan king with a high black topknot, gold forehead band, indigo angarakha over cream sleeves, quilted brown vest, brick-red sash, ochre trousers, maroon shawl and a curved Deccan sword at his left hip, while Karka II is a dignified Rashtrakuta ruler with a lower black knot, modest conical crown, off-white dhoti with green border, mustard tunic, deep-green shawl, refined gold jewellery and a rolled palm-leaf charter bound with red cord.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two contrasting 10th-century Deccan kings, Tailapa II and Karka II, standing side by side in the same scene so their designs can be redrawn consistently: Tailapa is a lean, battle-hardened man in his late 30s with a narrow face, medium-brown complexion, a faint scar on his left cheek and intense eyes, his long black hair tied into a high warrior topknot with a dark-red cloth band and a narrow gold forehead strip; he wears a deep-indigo, knee-length angarakha-style tunic crossing left over right over a cream, long-sleeved inner shirt, a wide brick-red sash tightly around his waist, straight ankle-length dull-ochre trousers, a sleeveless quilted brown cotton vest with vertical stitching, and dark-brown leather sandals, with a deep-maroon shawl edged in mustard draped from his left shoulder across his chest and back, modestly covering his torso while leaving his arms free; his jewellery is simple gold disc earrings, a rudraksha-style bead necklace and slim gold bangles, and his signature curved single-edged Deccan sword in a dark-brown leather scabbard hangs from his left hip on a plain belt. Beside him, Karka is a slightly broader, dignified man in his early 30s with a medium-brown complexion, a slightly rounder face and calm, proud eyes; his long black hair is pulled into a lower, thicker knot wrapped with a pale-gold band and topped with a modest conical cloth-covered crown cap with a small central red stone; he wears an off-white ankle-length cotton dhoti with a wide dark-green geometric border, a light-mustard long-sleeved waist-length tunic with a round neck and maroon-edged cuffs, and a rich deep-green uttariya shawl draped over both shoulders and diagonally across his chest, along with dark-tan leather sandals; his jewellery includes medium gold disc earrings, a short gold necklace with three small pendants, narrow engraved gold armlets and broader wrist bangles, and his signature prop is a rolled, polished palm-leaf charter bound with a red cord that he holds or tucks under his arm; keep the palette dominated by deep indigo, brick red, mustard, off-white and deep green, with clear, consistent facial features, hairstyles, garments and accessories shown front-on in a clean, neutral pose for both characters.
